practices.practice: Read the cluster connection URI from an environment variable (e.g., process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI) and do not commit credentials to source control; use a secrets store for production.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DOCUMENTDB_URI from an environment variable at runtime; never commit it to source control. Provide a .env.example with a placeholder and document using an Azure Key Vault secret or other secrets store for production.

practices.practice: Create a single shared MongoClient (singleton) for the process and tune connection-pool options (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) appropriate to serverless vs long-running servers.
practices.prior_belief: Use a singleton, shared Mongoose/MongoClient connection for the whole app instead of creating a new connection per request. Configure connection pool size (e.g., maxPoolSize), socketTimeoutMS and serverSelectionTimeoutMS in the connection options.

practices.practice: Require TLS on all client connections to Azure DocumentDB (include tls=true and keep certificate validation enabled); do not disable TLS verification in production.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL for client connections and include tls=true (or tls=true&tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) in the connection string; do not disable certificate validation in production.

practices.practice: Implement retries for transient network and rate errors with exponential backoff, enable driver retryReads/retryWrites where appropriate, and for transaction work use an explicit retry loop per MongoDB transaction retry guidance.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry with exponential backoff for transient network and server selection errors (MongoNetworkError, MongoServerSelectionError, retryable write errors). For non-idempotent operations use idempotency tokens or avoid automatic retry; for transactions, only retry entire transaction logic according to MongoDB transaction retry guidance (explicit retry loop with new session).

practices.practice: Protect against duplicate postings by creating a unique (or partial unique) index on transactions.idempotencyKey and using upsert/$setOnInsert or catching duplicate-key errors to return the existing result.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce idempotency by creating a unique index on transactions.idempotencyKey (e.g., db.transactions.createIndex({idempotencyKey:1}, {unique:true, partialFilterExpression:{idempotencyKey:{$exists:true}}})). Use upsert/findOneAndUpdate with $setOnInsert or insert within a transaction and handle duplicate key errors gracefully.

practices.practice: If you only need idempotency for a bounded window, make idempotency records compact and expire them with a TTL index on a Date field (expireAfterSeconds), remembering TTL uses a Date field and deletions are not instantaneous.
practices.prior_belief: Make idempotency records compact and immutable (idempotencyKey, clientId, createdAt, responseRef). Use a TTL index if you only need idempotency for a bounded window (e.g., expire idempotency keys after configurable hours/days).

practices.practice: Write compact, targeted aggregation pipelines: $match as early as possible, project only necessary fields, use allowDiskUse:true for large groupings, and verify pipeline performance with explain("executionStats").
practices.prior_belief: Use compact, targeted aggregation pipelines: $match early, project only necessary fields, use indexes for $match/$sort, and set allowDiskUse:true for large groupings. Verify pipeline performance with explain() and use indexes to satisfy early $match stages.

practices.practice: Use explain("executionStats") and index stats to monitor index usage and confirm queries are using intended indexes (watch keysExamined/docsExamined vs nReturned), and avoid over-indexing write-hot collections to reduce write amplification and RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor indexes with explain() and the cluster tools to ensure aggregation stages use the expected index; create covered indexes for heavy read paths and avoid over-indexing write-hot collections to reduce write amplification and RU costs.

practices.practice: Design compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) and create a compound index for common ledger queries such as account history (e.g., accountId first, then timestamp for sorting), to avoid COLLSCAN and in-memory sorts.
practices.prior_belief: Create an index on transactions.accountId and a compound index for common query patterns (e.g., {accountId:1, timestamp:-1, currency:1}) so balance and history queries are covered and avoid full-collection scans.

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON document limit and avoid unbounded arrays in a single document by splitting large or growing fields into separate collections.
practices.prior_belief: Limit document size (MongoDB document limit ~16MB) and design transactions so they don't accumulate large in-memory operations; paginate large result sets and use streaming/cursors for large exports.

practices.practice: For vector search use the cluster's cosmosSearch vector indexes: prefer vector-diskann for large production collections (M30+), use HNSW for moderate sizes, set correct dimensions and similarity, and normalize embeddings for cosine similarity.
practices.prior_belief: If leveraging vector capabilities (embeddings) do not index high-dimensional vectors with B-tree indexes; use the cluster’s vector index types (HNSW/IVF) with appropriate dimension, metric (cosine/inner), and index parameters (efConstruction, M or nlist) and control query 'ef'/'probe' for recall/latency tradeoffs.

practices.practice: Use Azure DocumentDB full-text search via createSearchIndexes and the $search aggregation stage (BM25 scoring) rather than the community $text path; create search indexes with definition.mappings and target them by name when querying.

Default to a single-shard collection; shard only when a collection's storage or throughput exceeds one physical shard's budget and choose the shard key to localize reads or to evenly distribute writes depending on workload.

Enable in-region high availability (HA) for production clusters to get automatic failover and the 99.99% SLA and consider cross-region replicas for DR/read scale-out when a higher SLA or cross-region availability is required.

When you need to expire data (sessions, caches, short-lived idempotency records), use TTL indexes on a Date field and remember TTL indices are single-field, non-compound and deletions are performed by a background sweeper at ~60s granularity.
Split schema responsibilities: embed small bounded subdocuments read together, but reference or move unbounded child collections to their own collection to avoid growth and rewrite amplification.

Use explain("executionStats") on find and aggregate operations (including $match and $sort) to detect COLLSCANs, high docsExamined/keysExamined ratios, and scatter-gather plans and iterate index design accordingly.
For production vector indexes, store embedding metadata (model name, dims, version) with the vector so you can detect model drift and perform re-embeds when the model or normalization changes.

Prefer creating a tuned compound index that matches the common query prefix rather than many overlapping single-field indexes; use index lifecycle (hide → monitor → drop) before dropping to avoid surprises.
When evaluating queries or adding indexes in CI, assert explain-metrics (e.g., totalDocsExamined / nReturned) for critical queries to detect regressions before deploy.
